correctness.rationale: The proof uses the exact polar description of a symmetric edge polytope as a graph Lipschitz polytope and the published complete wheel-facet word classification. After fixing the cone label to zero, centering a word with p positive and q negative entries gives squared normal norm p+q-(p-q)^2/(m+1). If both signs occur, cyclic separation forces at least two zeros; for fixed nonzero count the norm is maximized by balancing the signs, and the resulting parity-dependent objective strictly increases until exactly two zeros remain. A separate concave bound proves every one-sign word is strictly worse for m at least five. Equality forces exactly one positive block and one negative block separated by the two zeros, yielding the stated orbit counts. Central symmetry justifies using the centered polar circumradius to compute the global inradius.

value.rationale: Wheel graphs are singled out in the motivating symmetric-edge-polytope source as an important and enumeratively challenging family tied to the Kuramoto model. The theorem adds a basic intrinsic Euclidean invariant for every non-small wheel, reveals a genuine even/odd phase law, and identifies the complete set of closest facet orbits. Through polarity it simultaneously evaluates a natural graph-spread invariant. This is an all-dimensions structural calculation, not a finite table or arbitrary parameter slice.
